description_for_human: Discover current federal opportunities and research historical private-foundation funding prospects.
description_for_model: MANDATORY: Call search_grants for every new grant discovery, recommendation, ranking, or comparison request. Pass the user's complete natural-language request in query so the server can derive the correct mission, geography, population, and only award constraints the user actually stated; never replace it with the demo profile or generic keywords. Never invent or default project.estimatedBudget, filters.minimumAward, or filters.maximumAward. If the user gives no budget or desired award amount, omit all three so GrantPilot searches every award size. Recommend only sufficiently relevant records returned by the tool, and explicitly report when fewer records match instead of padding the requested count with unrelated opportunities. Preserve the search tool's standardized sections and list every returned-page record one by one; do not reduce the response to a few notable examples. If the user does not request an exact count, omit requestedResultCount so GrantPilot uses its 80-result default; never invent 10 as a generic default. Pass requestedResultCount only when the user's prompt contains an exact count. The supported range is 1–100, and requests above 100 must receive the tool's explicit limit response rather than silent truncation. When the user asks for more or next results, call load_more_grants with the prior queryId and nextOffset; never start a new 10-result search. Respect requested resultTypes exactly: current-federal, forecasted-federal, and historical-private-prospect. Never include historical-private-prospect when the user asks for current grants only or excludes historical results. Recommend and name only records returned by the tool; never add funders or programs from general knowledge. When the user asks to learn more about a named result, call get_grant_details and explain the overview, why it matches, main eligibility concern, geographic evidence, score breakdown, and next verification steps without asking the user to type that framework. When the user asks to compare selected records, call compare_grants and provide a decision-focused comparison of eligibility, mission, geography, award fit, deadline/capacity, cost share, application effort, confidence, risks, and missing facts, ending with a primary pursuit, backup, and verification checklist. Present Grants.gov opportunities separately from IRS 990-PF historical prospects. Frame IRS 990-PF records positively and concisely as: Evidence-backed potential private donor/funder candidates worth researching and possibly contacting. USAspending is historical federal-award context only. Never claim that eligibility or funding is guaranteed.
